meta: Whatever you paste into an AI chat is sent to the AI company's servers and often stored. This video shows what you shouldn't paste, and a simple trick to still get help safely.

muc.title: Pasting your whole customer file?
muc.text: You ask AI to write an email to a customer, and you paste a whole table of names, phone numbers and account numbers. Wait a moment.

muc.title: Where what you type goes
muc.text: What you type is sent to the AI company's servers and is often stored. Depending on the service and your settings, it may also be used to train AI.

muc.title: What not to give AI
muc.text: Don't paste passwords, one-time codes (OTP), card numbers, ID numbers, health records, customer data or confidential company documents.

muc.title: You can still ask, just hide the details
muc.text: You can still get help from AI. Just replace real details with placeholders: a name becomes "Customer A", an amount becomes "X".

muc.title: Fill in the real details afterwards
muc.text: Once AI writes the draft, you fill the real details back in yourself. Same result, and your real data never leaves your device.

muc.title: Check your privacy settings
muc.text: Also, open the privacy settings of the AI app you use, see what it stores, and turn off what you don't want. If your company has its own AI rules, follow them.

muc.title: Ten seconds before you paste
muc.text: Next time you ask AI for help with real information, take ten seconds to change names to "Customer A" and amounts to "X" before you paste.
